study_type_evidence.quote: we established two subcutaneous xenograft mouse models of prostate cancer with C4-2 cells (5 × 106, AR-positive) and CWR22rv1 cells
We have conducted in vivo mouse pharmacokinetics assay for the peptide PROTAC drug with/without Au with intraperitoneal injection.
we suspended the Au-AR DBD PROTAC drug and free AR DBD PROTAC drug separately in PBS containing 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS)
we treated C4-2, LNCaP, and CWR22Rv1 cells with the Au-AR DBD PROTAC drug at concentrations ranging from 10 to 1000 nM

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: nude mice bearing C4-2 or CWR22Rv1 subcutaneous xenografts; sex and age not reported
in_vivo_species.quote: Tumor growth curves of C4-2 xenografts in nude mice treated as indicated (n = 5 per group).

ex_vivo_detail: Serum-stability testing of free AR pep-PROTAC and Au-AR pep-PROTAC in PBS containing 10% fetal bovine serum (bovine-derived serum), with time-dependent changes measured by RP-HPLC. Classified as ex vivo because it is a serum-stability assay.
in_vitro_detail: Cell-line work in C4-2, LNCaP, CWR22Rv1, VCaP, DU145, PC-3, MCF-7, T47D, 293T and AML 12 cells (viability, immunoblot degradation, immunoprecipitation, ubiquitination, immunofluorescence); isothermal titration calorimetry with recombinant MDM2, MDMX, AR-V7 and AR ΔDBD; fluorescence polarization of rhodamine B-labelled AR DBD; hERG assay on cardiac muscle cells; pH 3.0/5.0/7.4 buffer stability; glutathione (10 mM) release assay.

agents.name: Au-AR pep-PROTAC (AR pep-PROTAC drug loaded onto ultrasmall gold nanoparticles)
agents.sequence: YLCSSNNNRERDKFRRGGSGGTSFEQFWAWLWP (AR DBD-targeting sequence + GGSGG flexible linker + MDM2-targeting sequence; conjugated to Au nanoparticles through the cysteine via a gold-thiol bond, with branched PEI)
agents.sequence_source: RESULTS body text: "we obtained the designed peptide PROTAC sequence: YLCSSNNNRERDKFRRGGSGGTSFEQFWAWLWP"
agents.group_n: n = 5 mice per group in the xenograft efficacy studies; group size for the pharmacokinetic study is not reported
agents.group_n_quote: Treatment of five groups of mice (5 mice per group) was initiated (i.e., day 1) after tumors were established
agents.dose: 2 mg/kg, dissolved at 0.4 mg/ml in PBS, 100 µl per injection (efficacy studies); dose for the ICP-MS pharmacokinetic study is not reported
agents.route: subcutaneous injection in C4-2 models and intraperitoneal injection in CWR22rv1 models; intraperitoneal injection for the pharmacokinetic study
agents.dose_route_quote: Two administration routes were tested in the xenograft models, with subcutaneous injection (SC.) in C4-2 models and intraperitoneal injection (IP.) in CWR-22rv1 models.
agents.half_life_matrix: mouse, in vivo (gold quantified by ICP-MS); a separate ex vivo half-life of 25.1 h was measured in PBS containing 10% serum
agents.pk_quote: PK analysis of Au-AR DBD PROTAC was performed by ICP-MS. As depicted in Figures 6C and S23 ... the t1/2 of Au-AR DBD PROTAC is 26.3 h.

agents.name: Free AR pep-PROTAC (unconjugated peptide PROTAC)
agents.dose: not reported (biodistribution comparison after rhodamine B labelling); dose for the intraperitoneal PK comparison not reported
agents.dose_route_quote: We have conducted in vivo mouse pharmacokinetics assay for the peptide PROTAC drug with/without Au with intraperitoneal injection.
agents.half_life_matrix: PBS containing 10% serum (ex vivo serum-stability assay quantified by HPLC)
agents.pk_quote: The half-life of the free AR pep-PROTAC drug was only 1.9 h, while the half-life of the Au-AR pep-PROTAC was 25.1 h.

agents.name: Bare Au nanoparticles
agents.group_n_quote: 25 tumor-bearing mice were randomly divided into 5 groups and treated every three days for three weeks
agents.dose: 2 mg/kg (same dose as the other arms)
agents.dose_route_quote: treated every three days for three weeks with PBS, bare Au nanoparticles, the Au-AR pep-PROTAC drug, Au-Peptide Control, or enzalutamide at the same dose (2 mg kg−1)

agents.name: Au-Peptide Control (reversal peptide-loaded Au nanoparticles)
agents.sequence: not reported (described only as the 'reversal peptide' of the AR pep-PROTAC sequence)
agents.group_n_quote: Treatment of five groups of mice (5 mice per group) was initiated (i.e., day 1) after tumors were established
agents.dose_route_quote: All the drug including Au-AR pep-PROTAC drug, Au-Peptide Control and enzalutamide were dissolved in 0.4 mg ml−1 in PBS (pH 7.4).

agents.name: Enzalutamide
agents.group_n_quote: Tumor growth curves of CWR22Rv1 xenografts in nude mice (n = 5 per group).
agents.dose_route_quote: treated every three days for three weeks with PBS, bare Au nanoparticles, the Au-AR pep-PROTAC drug, Au-Peptide Control, or enzalutamide at the same dose (2 mg kg−1)

agents.name: PBS (pH 7.4)
agents.group_n_quote: 25 tumor-bearing mice were randomly divided into 5 groups
agents.dose_route_quote: Each injection volume was 100 µl and PBS was used as control.

agents.name: ARV-110
agents.dose: not reported for this study (cited prior animal dosage of 1 or 3 mg/kg)
agents.route: in cellulo comparison only in this study
agents.dose_route_quote: Taking ARV-110 (clinical trial II) as a representative control, we compared its efficacy with this Au-AR pep-PROTAC in cellulo.

concentration_time_figure.locator: Fig. 6C (in vivo PK by ICP-MS); Fig. 2E (ex vivo serum stability)
concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: C) Pharmacokinetics analysis of Au-AR pep-PROTAC by ICP-MS.
concentration_time_figure.note: Fig. 6C is the in vivo pharmacokinetic profile from which t1/2 = 26.3 h was derived. Fig. 2E is a serum-stability plot of residual drug versus time in PBS with 10% FBS (half-lives 1.9 h free peptide, 25.1 h Au-conjugated). Fig. 6B shows biodistribution at different time points.

bioanalytical_method: ICP-MS (gold quantification) for in vivo pharmacokinetics; reversed-phase HPLC for serum stability, glutathione-triggered release and pH stability; rhodamine B fluorescence imaging for biodistribution
bioanalytical_quote: PK analysis of Au-AR DBD PROTAC was performed by ICP-MS.
notes: The pharmacokinetic dose, dosing volume and number of animals for the ICP-MS study are not reported in the body. There is an internal inconsistency in the dosing schedule: Results state treatment 'every three days for three weeks' whereas Methods state 'a 3-week treatment regimen with an injection every other day'. The reported 26.3 h half-life is for gold measured by ICP-MS, i.e. it tracks the nanoparticle rather than the intact peptide. The statement that 'the half-life of majority free peptides is <5 h' is attributed to publications, not measured here. Mechanistic tool compounds used only in vitro (cycloheximide, MG132, nutlin-3, DHT, MDM2 siRNA) are not listed as agents. No Cmax or Tmax is reported.
